FSQ-only future qualification and single-attempt campaign gates. No Android,
FSQ, AMKernel or Appium module is imported by the offline consumers. Live
subcommands require independently reviewed, target-exclusive authorization.
Qualification consumes existing apps/snapshots: it never installs, repairs,
saves a replacement snapshot, or invents a first-launch UI recipe. Rehearsal
is a separate non-scoring official lifecycle check, not evidence that the FSQ
policy succeeds.

method.campaign: Use only existing offline fixture factories from tests/test_fsq_campaign.py via runpy, call candidate.__wrapped__ with a temporary root/MonkeyPatch context, mutate indicated consumer data, recompute affected references/artifact rows/seal, invoke actual operational_errors or validate_stage_report. No pytest test functions were run.
method.killAndForcedArchive: Use only offline_episode.__wrapped__ from tests/test_fsq_runner.py, replace native-worker output or archival boundary, invoke actual run_episode, inspect actual terminal record and halt_reason. This does not claim a real full-native execution.
method.sandbox: Invoke /usr/bin/sandbox-exec using actual generated policy and native FSQ interpreter/FileOps.read_text; construct canonical relative traversal to retained source and temporary external private sentinel; compare denied evaluator-site file. Never publish oracle text.
method.processGroup: Actual _supervise starts only throwaway Python leader/child; child ignores SIGTERM, leader does not; observe child state then kill only that owned group and confirm removal.
method.standalone: Separate throwaway Python process uses offline fixture admission/environment, actual fsq_runner.main argv and run_episode, a shortened injected episode allocator and blocking initialize_task; externally terminate only its owned group after the bound is exceeded.
